paragraphs: Islington Council has its own fostering service, and children in its care may also live with independent agencies such as those on this page. Fostering recruitment for Islington, along with Barnet, Camden, Enfield, Hackney and Haringey, is now provided through the North London Fostering Hub, which Camden leads and which launched on 1 October 2026.

Islington welcomes carers of all ages and backgrounds, single or in a relationship, with or without children of their own, working or on benefits, and whether they own or rent. You need a spare bedroom to foster a child over two, good general health, spoken and written English, and the time to take children to school, appointments and family time.

Preparation is a free four-day Skills to Foster course held in Islington, followed by core training in areas such as therapeutic parenting, trauma-informed practice and safeguarding. Carers have a social worker who visits regularly, a duty team available all day, every day, monthly support groups and automatic membership of the Islington Foster Carers Association. The council says it pays the council tax of foster carers who live in the borough, pays for Fostering Network membership and offers a £1,500 thank-you payment if someone you refer is approved.
Allowance figures are not on the pages we read, so ask the council and two or three of the agencies below for theirs and compare the support each one gives.

sources.title: Camden chosen to lead new North London Fostering Hub (Camden Council)
